Support the `npu_scatter_nd_update_sk` custom operator on Ascend950

[Feature]Support using fused operators to improve performance of layerwise sparse offload (#17392)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Relies on PR #16640 for kernels.

This PR introduces 2 new kernels `fused_lightning_indexer_manage` and

sparse offload in decode phase. Compared to the original workflow:

```
LI -> LRU selection -> Sparse Onload -> SFA
```

Now we have:

```
LIM -> Copy_SFA
```

`bind_connector_meatadata`. This mainly aligns to vLLM PR

[Feature][EPLB] Support policy-prepared temporal load statistics (#17509)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This is PR 2 of the STAIR EPLB series described in
vllm-project/vllm-ascend#17506. It adds a policy-neutral contract for
bounded temporal load statistics:

- policies may prepare fixed-shape values plus optional sample weights;
- rank-local phase gaps remain aligned on one shared time axis;
- samples from a previous mapping generation are discarded;
- physical-expert samples are mapped to logical experts before
publication;
- empty windows become safe no-op cycles; and
- the complete snapshot is published atomically through the existing
async worker lifecycle.

Policies without `prepare_local_load_stats` retain the upstream/default
path. This PR contains no STAIR planner and starts from the common
series baseline `9f1af00c7fcd7c22cf0c791ab9f6c8d98402ec06`.

Refs vllm-project/vllm-ascend#17506.
Refs vllm-project/vllm#49702.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No by itself. The new temporal statistics path is activated only by a
policy that implements the preparation hook; the default policy remains
unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- `bash format.sh ci`
- 14 focused CPU unit tests passed.
- Added tests for skipped samples, stale-generation reset, logical
aggregation, empty windows, atomic publication, and default-path
behavior.

[Feature][EPLB] Add constrained STAIR placement (#17512)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This is PR 5 of the STAIR EPLB series described in
vllm-project/vllm-ascend#17506. It extends the pure CPU planner from
#17511 with constrained, deterministic placement and migration-source
selection:

- covariance-aware LPT placement with bounded backtracking;
- incremental replica-count changes from the committed placement;
- per-rank send/receive budgets and per-node cross-node budgets;
- `-1` unlimited budgets for high-bandwidth systems and `0` to disable
cross-node transfers;
- topology-aware source selection and stable source-slot alignment;
- zero-redundancy physical expert swaps;
- mean and p95 non-regression acceptance; and
- fixed-shape plan validation before execution.

Feasibility results are cached across beam candidates and rank scoring
is vectorized to bound planner overhead. The branch starts from the same
series baseline, `9f1af00c7fcd7c22cf0c791ab9f6c8d98402ec06`, and is
intentionally stacked on #17511 so the placement code can reuse its
load, risk, and replica types.

Depends on #17511.
Refs vllm-project/vllm-ascend#17506.
Refs vllm-project/vllm#33549.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

It adds advanced STAIR transfer-budget controls, but does not select or
execute STAIR by itself. Existing EPLB policies remain unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- `bash format.sh ci`
- 62 focused CPU tests passed across STAIR policy and configuration
coverage.
- Tests cover deterministic placement, covariance, bounded backtracking,
zero-redundancy swaps, rank and node budgets, unlimited budgets,
topology preference, incremental replica changes, mean/p95 gates, and
plan validation.

The PR remains draft until the RFC and dependent planner interface are
reviewed. Real NPU integration is exercised by the final integration PR.

[Feature][EPLB] Add STAIR load and replica planning (#17511)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This is PR 4 of the STAIR EPLB series described in
vllm-project/vllm-ascend#17506. It adds the pure CPU load-modeling and
replica
planning half of STAIR:

- loss-aware chronological compression with exact bin weights;
- weighted expert mean, sample variance, and covariance;
- risk-adjusted expert load using a configurable normal quantile;
- weighted mean and nearest-rank p95 imbalance metrics;
- nonzero-load, relative-hysteresis, and absolute-balance gates; and
- deterministic bounded FlashTree-style replica-count search.

Search controls have validated static bounds and conservative defaults.
The
planner is independent of model-runner state, device collectives, and
transfer
execution. This branch starts from the common series baseline
`9f1af00c7fcd7c22cf0c791ab9f6c8d98402ec06`.

Refs vllm-project/vllm-ascend#17506.
Refs vllm-project/vllm#33549.

It defines advanced STAIR tuning fields, but does not select or execute
STAIR
by itself. Existing EPLB policies remain unchanged.

- 28 focused CPU tests passed.
- Tests cover weighted compression equivalence, covariance, zero/single
samples, quantile and configuration bounds, placement imbalance,

[Feature][EC Transfer] Add MemCache-backed L1 encoder cache (#16953)

[Feature][EC Transfer] Add MemCache-backed L1 encoder cache
### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR introduces `ECMemcacheConnector`, a MemCache-backed L1 cache
for multimodal encoder outputs. It integrates with vLLM through the
existing EC connector framework and uses the multimodal feature
identifier (`mm_hash`) as the cache key.

Repeated image or video inputs can reuse previously computed encoder
embeddings instead of running the multimodal encoder again.

- Add a scheduler-side MemCache client that checks multiple `mm_hash`
  values in one request and records cache hits and misses.
- Send per-step load/save metadata from the scheduler to workers:
  cache hits are loaded from MemCache, while misses run the encoder and
  publish the resulting embeddings.
- Load multiple encoder outputs directly into preallocated NPU tensors
  with `batch_get_into`.
- Use `KeyInfo.size()` together with the model dtype and encoder hidden
  dimension to reconstruct each cached tensor as
  `[num_encoder_tokens, hidden_dim]`.
- Publish newly computed encoder outputs directly from NPU memory with
  `put_from`.
- Record an NPU event before dispatching the put operation to a
background
  thread, so MemCache waits for encoder computation without blocking the
  model-runner thread.
- Save only from TP rank 0 and PCP rank 0. Encoder outputs are identical
across TP/PCP ranks, so publishing from every rank would duplicate data
  and cause concurrent writes to the same `mm_hash`.
- Keep eviction management inside MemCache. The connector does not add a
  separate local eviction policy.
- Track cumulative cache hits, misses, and hit rate for debugging and
  observability.

This PR also extends MemcacheBackend with:
- batch_get_into, for copying multiple values into flat destination
  buffers.
- put_from, for publishing one value directly from a device buffer.
- Optional transfer-direction arguments for the existing get and put
  wrappers while preserving their previous default directions.
When the connector is not configured, the existing encoder execution and
cache behavior remain unchanged.

Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
Yes, when ECMemcacheConnector is explicitly enabled.

The connector can be enabled without modifying vLLM:

```bash
vllm serve <model> \
  --ec-transfer-config '{
     "ec_connector": "ECMemcacheConnector",
     "ec_connector_module_path": "vllm_ascend.distributed.ec_transfer.ec_memcache_connector",
     "ec_role": "ec_both",
  "ec_connector_extra_config": {
     "recv_buffer_tokens": 8192
  }
}'
```

commits.message:
[BugFix][MRV2][P/D] Fix MRV2 kv_caches_dict register_kv_caches only use first tensor (#17522)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Fix MRV2 initialization and KV-cache handling for Ascend’s per-layer K/V
tuples and Conv/SSM lists. The previous workaround returned only the
first tensor to satisfy upstream device filtering, dropping V/SSM from
connector registration and breaking PD transfer.

Flatten only the runner’s internal cache list while preserving the
complete cache dictionary for model bindings and connectors. Reuse the
existing Ascend block-copy implementation and adapt MRV2 metadata to the
existing Ascend zeroer, leaving MRV1 unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No.

### How was this patch tested?
By CI.
